summary: Stella Kramrisch specialized in Indology and art history, earning her Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Josef Strzygowski and Max Dvořák. She held posts at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, the Courtauld Institute, the Philadelphia Museum of Art, NYU, and Penn.

Stella Sandahl is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Armand Minard. She held academic posts at the Sorbonne and at the University of Toronto, where she served as professor (attested 2003–2017).

Sten Konow was a Norwegian scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at Oslo and Halle under Richard Pischel, he held professorships at Oslo and Hamburg, and worked for the Archaeological Survey of India.

Stephan Licha works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After earning his PhD from SOAS University of London in 2012, he held postdoctoral positions at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo, and joined the University of Chicago faculty (attested 2026).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephan V. Beyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Rochester and under Richard Hugh Robinson, served as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1972–1979), and later worked at Sidley Austin.

Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oberlin, Stanford, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry, as well as under Thich Nhat Hanh. She served as professor at the University of Vermont (1991–2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar in Tibetology who completed her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist who completed her doctorate at Yale under Stanley Insler and Warren Crawford Cowgill. She held posts at Harvard University (~1986–1989, ~1996–2002, attested 2008) and UCLA (~2002).

Stephen Addiss was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who completed his master's and doctorate at the University of Michigan. He held professorships at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and the University of Richmond (1992–2013).

Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher who studied at various traditional centers under teachers including Geshe Rabten and Kusan Sunim. He founded and directed Sharpham College (~1992–2000) and joined Bodhi College as core faculty (~2015).

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. After earning his Ph.D. at UC Santa Barbara in 1999, he became an associate professor of religious studies at Missouri State University.

Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religion who earned his doctorate from Princeton in 1986. After teaching at Middlebury College (~1986–1988), he returned to Princeton in 1988 as professor.

Stephen Fuchs was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna. He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, founded the Anthropos Institute, and directed the Institute of Indian Culture from 1967.

Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University under Jacqueline I. Stone (~1996–2001) and held a post at Western Michigan University starting around 2003.
Stephen H. Phillips is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who served as professor (attested 1995–1999) and later professor emeritus (attested 2020–2026) at the University of Texas at Austin.
Stephen Harris is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of New Mexico in 2014 and became an assistant professor at Leiden University that same year.
Stephen Hislop was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1834–1838), the University of Glasgow (~1838–1840), and under Thomas Chalmers (~1840–1844).
Stephen Hodge is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held a post at the University of London (attested 2000) and is attested as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg in 2026.

Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Notre Dame in 1991 and joined the University of St. Thomas philosophy department as an associate professor in 1990.
